title: IaC module compatibility matrix and version pinning for Private VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Goal: Produce a clear compatibility matrix and concrete version-pinning policy for Terraform core, first-party providers, and Redwood IaC modules that are used for Private/VPC deployments. Deliverables: 1) a markdown compatibility matrix checked into infra/docs/, 2) a set of recommended 'required_version' and 'required_providers' lines for each module root, 3) CI automation that enforces pins and regenerates provider lockfiles, 4) an upgrade runbook and staged health-check suite for module/provider upgrades. Motivation: We observed drift and spurious plan diffs across customer Private deployments when different teams used different Terraform/Provider versions. This ticket scopes the automation and documentation needed to make upgrades predictable and safe for Dedicated/Private customers. Scope includes networking modules (vpc, subnets, route-tables), bootstrap modules (iam, kms), and cluster modules (k8s, node pools). Out of scope for this ticket: changing any production resource semantics — those belong to separate module change PRs. Success = documented matrix + CI enforcement + successful canary upgrade in our staging account.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix document added: infra/docs/iac-compatibility-matrix.md and linked from private-vpc runbook
Each module root contains a 'recommended-pins.tf' example with required_version and required_providers lines
CI job 'iac-pins-check' fails if infra repo contains provider or core versions outside the supported matrix
Provider lockfiles (terraform.lock.hcl) are generated and committed for modules that are published to the module registry
Runbook 'infra/runbooks/vpc-upgrade.md' created with step-by-step canary upgrade instructions
Automated health-checks (smoke tests + Terraform plan/diff check) pass in staging after a module/provider bump
technical_notes: Recommendation: adopt constrained ranges instead of exact pins where safe. Example: terraform { required_version = ">= 1.4, < 1.7" } and provider "aws" { source = "hashicorp/aws" version = "~> 4.60" }
Use terraform providers lock -platform for supported CI platforms to ensure deterministic plugins across runners
For modules published internally, include a pinned terraform.lock.hcl in the module distribution and use 'module_override' patterns in downstream stacks where needed
Major-version bumps (e.g., aws provider 4.x -> 5.x) require an explicit module change PR with automated migration tests; do not allow range wildcards across major boundaries
Keep an explicit mapping section: module X vA is tested against providers {aws: 4.60, kubernetes: 2.15} and terraform core 1.5.x
We will surface provider deprecation warnings in CI by running 'terraform plan' with TF_LOG=TRACE in a non-blocking preflight step
Implement an 'upgrade-candidate' branch job that applies upgrades to a disposable staging workspace and runs the health-check suite before merging

risks: Pinning too strictly may block small teams from making necessary minor upgrades; mitigate with documented exceptions and a short approval path
Provider major upgrades carry resource-change risk (eg. semantic resource renames) that cannot be fully validated in unit tests; require canary in disposable staging
Committing terraform.lock.hcl for modules increases merge conflicts when multiple module authors update providers simultaneously
Customers with older private stacks may have custom forks that expect older provider behavior — coordinate cutover windows and provide a compatibility shim
rollback_plan: If a canary upgrade causes test failures, revert the module/provider bump commit, run terraform apply with previous lockfile in the staging workspace, and notify impacted owners. For production incidents, promote emergency rollback PR that pins the previous known-good provider versions and run the documented rollback checklist in infra/runbooks/vpc-upgrade.md.

Safety: automated 'drift detection' job validates that post-upgrade terraform plan is empty for 48 hours
